 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 31.10.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Ramdurg (for short, 'tribunal') in MVC No.765/2017

M.F.A no.101278/2019 is filed by insurer for reduction of compensation while M.F.A. no.102629/2019 is filed by claimant for enhancement.
2. Occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to its rash and negligent driving and claimant sustaining injuries therein is not in dispute.
Claimant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for compensation against owner and insurer of offending vehicle.

3. On contest, Tribunal passed award holding insurer liable to pay compensation of Rs.9,22,441/-
with interest at rate of 9% per annum.
4. Shri R.R.Mane, learned counsel for insurer submitted that claimant aged 22 years doing agriculturist sustained fracture of shaft of tibia and fibula.
Dr. Mahesh Umarani examined as PW2 though assessed limb disability at 50%, did not assess it to whole body.
Therefore, assessment of loss of earning capacity would be excessive.
Without taking note of said factor, Tribunal considered functional disability at 40% which was on higher side and sought reduction.

It was further submitted that award of rate of interest at 9% was also unsustainable and contrary to Section 34 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
5.

On other hand, Shri Chandrashekhar Hosamani, learned counsel for claimant-appellant submitted that accident occurred in year 2016 wherein claimant a 22 years old agriculturist sustained fracture of tibia and fibula.
Though he had stated that his income was Rs.15,000/- per month, Tribunal considered it at Rs.7,000/- which was inadequate and sought enhancement.

It was further submitted that considering fact that bone was still in unification process, assessment of disability was at a higher degree than in case of united fractures and therefore, no interference was sought for.
It was however submitted that award of compensation towards pain and suffering,

6. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused impugned judgment and award and the record.
7.
Insofar as monthly income

, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month,
same was not substantiated with evidence.
In absence, tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.
As per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for settlement of cases before Lok-Adalath, notional income for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/-.
Therefore, tribunal would not be justified in considering it at Rs.7,000/-.
Same has to be taken at Rs.8,750/- instead.
9. Insofar as extent of disability, Dr. Mahesh Umarani who had treated claimant was examined as PW2.
In his evidence, he stated that claimant sustained disability of 50% to limb as well as to whole body as fracture had not yet united.
Exhibit P20-disability certificate states that bone was in process of unification.
Under circumstances, considering whole body disability at 40% where limb disability was assessed at 50% would be grossly excessive.
In considered opinion of this Court and taking into account age and occupation of claimant, it would be appropriate to take loss of earning capacity at 25%.

Thus, future loss of income would be reassessed as follows:
"Rs.8,750/- x 25% x 12 x 18 = Rs.4,72,500/-."
10.
Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.
As claimant has sustained fracture of tibia and fibula, which appears adequate and does not call for interference.
Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.2,33,641/- towards medical expenses against bills produced.

Since,
same is in complete reimbursement of amount spent, there is no scope for enhancement.
11. From records as well as from observations of tribunal, claimant has taken inpatient treatment for 40 days.
Normally fractures take three months to heal.

Therefore, claimant would be entitled for award of compensation towards loss of income during laid up period for three months i.e.
Rs.26,250/- (Rs.8,750/- x 3).
12.
Likewise, award of Rs.20,000/- towards conveyance, attendant and other incidental charges would also be inadequate.
It would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.30,000/- under said head.
Taking into account fracture and disability assessed, award of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities would be grossly inadequate.
It would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.35,000/- towards same.
13. Since as per Exhibit P20 fracture is in process of unification, claimant would be required to take continuous treatment.
There are also implants inserted which would require removal.
